insider_note: A long definition to write nearly word for word. The phrase to include is 'at the industrial level'.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Biotechnology defined
steps.margin_note: The full definition. Five lines, and it is most of the answer.
lines: BIOTECHNOLOGY is the science that uses MICRO
ORGANISMS, or exploits CELLS and CELL
CONSTITUENTS, at the INDUSTRIAL LEVEL, to
make products useful to life and human welfare.
steps.why: The words 'industrial level' are what separate biotechnology from ordinary biology: the same processes, run at scale for a product.
common_mistakes: Leaving out 'industrial level'. Brewing beer in a kitchen is not biotechnology.
Saying biotechnology means genetic engineering only. Genetic engineering is one part of it.
steps.memory_tip: Living things put to work, at industrial scale.

steps.label: What it produces
steps.margin_note: Four or five named products, then the two core techniques.
lines: hormones such as insulin, industrial enzymes,
Genetic engineering and the maintenance of
sterile conditions are its two core techniques.
steps.why: Listing what it produces is the shortest way to show the definition was understood rather than memorised.
common_mistakes: Giving no examples. The second mark is for what it actually makes.
Naming only medicines. Crops and industrial enzymes are equally central.
steps.memory_tip: If a living thing made it and it is sold, it is biotechnology.
